def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (X Y : Type), Nonempty X → ∀ (Q : S1 X Y → Prop),
    (∀ N, N.D11 → Q N) → (∃ N, ¬ Q N) →
    ∀ c4 : (List X → Y) → Prop,
      ∃ N : S1 X Y, ¬ (Q N ↔ c4 N.d4)

translation:
Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition. For every pair of types X and Y, assuming X is nonempty, take any predicate Q on systems of type S1 X Y. Suppose (1) Q holds for every system whose finite node set is nonempty and in which every ordered pair of nodes m, n is connected by a directed path from m to n of at least one edge, and (2) there exists a system for which Q is false. In (1), an edge from m to n means that there exist two state assignments agreeing at every node other than m, and a common input x, such that the update at n gives different values for those assignments on x. The assignments need not be reachable. The path requirement includes m = n, so a zero-edge path does not suffice.

Under those hypotheses, for every predicate c4 on functions from finite lists of X to Y, there exists a system N of type S1 X Y such that exactly one of Q(N) and c4(N.d4) is true. Here N.d4 is the entire function that, on a list, starts at N’s initial state assignment, updates all nodes from the previous assignment on each input in order, and applies N’s output function to the final assignment. There is no list-length bound. The system witnessing the disagreement may depend on c4 and is not required to satisfy the path condition or to be the witness in (2).

divergences.description: The source's “Conversely” starts with a feedforward system. Lean does not even require that the nonconscious system's behaviour have a feedforward realization. In fact, Target requires every S1 behaviour to have a D11 realization: take Q to mean “my behaviour has a D11 realization.” If any behaviour lacked one, Q would meet both hypotheses yet be inferable exactly from the behaviour. This matters because N.d4 describes one system processing inputs online at all finite lengths. Such a system can retain an input bit indefinitely, which no finite acyclic S1 can do. Appendix A's construction starting from a feedforward implementation of x → F(x) does not state this result for arbitrary online behaviours.

As declared, D11 is a proxy for the consciousness-sufficient structure, not an IIT criterion. It requires the entire nonempty update-dependency graph to be strongly connected, with positive-length return paths, and counts dependencies even at unreachable states. The source's insertion of a ϕ-increasing device does not specify that graph condition.

Lean idealizes an inference as an arbitrary binary predicate on the complete behaviour function, whether or not an experiment could evaluate it. This is a natural strengthening of the source's indistinguishability point: identical functions agree under even these predicates.
Lean explicitly assumes an inhabited input type, as declared; the passage does not state that qualification.

judgement.summary: The disagreement conclusion has the advertised direction. The substantive difference is its scope: a converse construction on feedforward systems becomes a requirement that integrated systems cover every behaviour of an unrestricted-duration S1 system.
